sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Delivery Worker Atlas transforms data produced through the use of the Meu Corre App into collective information about app-based delivery work in Brazil. The project's methodology seeks to make transparent where the data come from, how they are processed, who is included in the analyzed base, how indicators are constructed, and what their limitations are.

Our goal is to produce reliable, useful, and accessible knowledge for workers, researchers, civil-society organizations, journalists, and public-policy makers, contributing to debate on platform work, urban mobility, and data justice.

Throughout this section, you will find detailed explanations of each stage of the process, the main concepts used in the analyses, and the methodological precautions adopted. Important terms such as regular user, net earnings, and working time are defined in the Glossary and can be consulted whenever necessary.

sections.title: Data provenance
paragraphs: Delivery Worker Atlas data are produced in different ways, always starting from workers' interaction with the Meu Corre App. This production includes information provided during registration, records made by workers themselves during their activity, geolocation data, data generated by use of the tool, and finally derived data created through calculations and processing.

These different sources of information are combined to form a robust and diversified analytical base, allowing platform work to be analyzed from multiple perspectives, from working time and urban circulation to earnings, expenses, and delivery workers' sociodemographic profile.

sections.title: Treatment and quality
sections.intro: Delivery Worker Atlas data go through a rigorous treatment process to ensure quality, consistency, and reliability. This process includes extraction, organization, standardization, validation, human review of information, as well as the treatment of incomplete data, atypical values, and open-text fields.

cards.title: Extraction and organization
cards.description: Data are extracted from records produced by workers themselves in Meu Corre. The information is then organized and standardized, harmonizing formats, units of measurement, and categories to allow comparisons across periods, territories, and delivery-worker profiles.

cards.title: Incomplete data and atypical values
cards.description: Incomplete data are treated using specific criteria, which may include excluding records, imputing values, or reclassifying categories, depending on the type of information. Atypical values are identified through statistical analysis and contextual review and may be retained, adjusted, or excluded according to their nature and impact on the analysis.

cards.title: Open text and human review
cards.description: Open-text fields, such as descriptions of places or workers' observations, are processed with language-processing techniques to standardize terms and categories, alongside human review of the information.

cards.title: Quality control
cards.description: Finally, systematic quality control is carried out, combining automated checks and human review to ensure the integrity of the analytical base used in research.

sections.title: Sample, scope, and biases
paragraphs: The Delivery Worker Atlas database is non-probabilistic and is formed through workers' voluntary adoption of the Meu Corre app. This means the sample is subject to self-selection biases and does not statistically represent the universe of platform delivery workers in Brazil.

Meu Corre users are not distributed uniformly across territories and delivery-worker profiles. There is a higher concentration of users in some regions, modes of transport, and activity ranges, which can influence analysis results.

Among the main identified biases are differences in users' professional profile and trajectories, variations in activity intensity, predominance of certain transport modes, and greater participation by workers who already have an interest in financial organization.

sections.title: Construction of the regular user
paragraphs: For many Delivery Worker Atlas analyses, we use the category of regular user, which identifies workers with continuous and minimally consistent participation in the database. This definition seeks to ensure greater temporal comparability and reduce the impact of sporadic records that can distort analyses of earnings, expenses, working time, and mobility patterns.

The regular-user category is constructed month by month using objective activity criteria in the app. As a result, the same worker may be considered regular in one month and not in another, depending on their level of activity during the period.

classificationSteps.title: Registered user
classificationSteps.description: Created an account in Meu Corre App.

classificationSteps.title: Active user
classificationSteps.description: Recorded at least one earning or expense in the period.

classificationSteps.title: Regular user
classificationSteps.description: Meets the three activity criteria in the reference month.

criteria.title: Registration before the reference month
criteria.description: The user must already have been registered in the app before the month being analyzed.

criteria.title: At least 5 earning and/or expense records
criteria.description: At least five earning or expense entries must have been recorded during the month.

criteria.title: Activity on at least 2 different days
criteria.description: Records must have occurred on two or more different days during the month.

note.title: Classification is monthly
note.description: The same user may be considered regular in one month and not in another, depending on their level of activity during the period.

sections.title: How to interpret the data
paragraphs: Delivery Worker Atlas data make it possible to observe characteristics, patterns, and changes in users' working conditions over time. The analyses can be used to understand trends, compare territories, modes of transport, and worker profiles, and identify differences across periods.

However, the DWA database was not constructed as a probabilistic sample and therefore does not allow estimation of the total number of delivery workers in Brazil or statistical generalizations for the entire category. It is important to consider methodological limitations and the context in which the data were produced when interpreting the results.

whatDataAllow.title: What the data allow
items: Analyze profiles and trajectories of Meu Corre App users.
Identify patterns and trends over time.
Compare indicators across territories, transport modes, and periods.
Explore relationships among earnings, expenses, working time, and urban circulation.
Support debates on working conditions, mobility, and public policy.

whatNotToInfer.title: What should not be inferred directly
items: The total number of delivery workers in Brazil.
Statistical representativeness of the sample for the entire category.
Direct comparisons with other studies without considering methodological differences.
Indicators for very small groups, which may not be stable or reliable.
